pajulahti.com zoominfo.com/c/pajulahti/369113600 Pajulahti Sports Institute is one of Finland's oldest and largest sports institutes, founded in 1929 and located on 110 hectares by Lake Iso-Kukkanen in Nastola (Lahti), about an hour from Helsinki. It is Finland's only official Olympic and Paralympic Training Center, known for its focus on endurance sports and paralympic athletics. Since January 2025, Pajulahti has been merged with Kisakallio and the Helsinki-based Urhea campus into Kolmen kampuksen urheiluopisto — the largest sports institute in Finland, with 3 campuses, ~200 employees, 73,000 m² of sports facilities, 320,000 visitors per year, and ~500 students in professional sports education. The merged group generates about €26 million in annual revenue, operates on a non-profit basis (owned by foundations)

dwmmh.org zoominfo.com/c/dw-mcmillan-memorial-hospital/77170917 D.W. McMillan Memorial Hospital is a small rural hospital in Brewton, Alabama, operating since 1954. It provides a 24/7 emergency room, ICU, surgery, obstetrics, outpatient chemotherapy, lab, imaging, and rehabilitation — serving as the main acute-care provider for the county. It has about 39–49 beds and employs roughly 85 staff, generating approximately $15 million in annual revenue. The hospital is part of a small county healthcare system that also runs clinics, EMS, and home health services. It has faced serious financial pressure — a $6 million deficit — but survived after county voters approved a tax increase in December 2025 expected to bring ~$1.8 million per year starting 2027.

crystalglassltd.co.uk Crystal Glass (Leeds) Ltd is a family-owned glass company based in Leeds, West Yorkshire, UK, founded in 1962 and officially registered as a limited company in 1974. It operates 5 branches — Leeds (HQ), Bradford, Harrogate, Wakefield, and Castleford — covering all of West Yorkshire. Its core services are 24/7/365 emergency glazing, double glazing replacement, and custom glasswork (shower screens, shopfronts, mirrors, partitions, and commercial facades). The company runs a lean family-managed SME model with roughly 10–25 employees and estimated revenue of £1–3 million per year

puroclean.com purocleanfranchise.com PuroClean is North America's largest privately owned property damage restoration franchise, known as "The Paramedics of Property Damage®", with 500+ franchise locations across the U.S., Canada, and Puerto Rico, headquartered in Tamarac, Florida. It provides 24/7 emergency services — water damage mitigation, fire and smoke restoration, mold remediation, biohazard cleanup, and reconstruction — responding within two hours, and is a preferred provider for 3 of the top 5 U.S. insurance carriers. The brand was launched in 2001 under the legal entity PuroSystems, LLC; in 2015 it was acquired by Mark W. Davis (former co-founder/CEO of Belfor North America) and Frank Torre, who grew the network from 222 to 500+ locations. The franchisor's audited revenue is $31.8 million (FY2025), while system-wide franchise sales exceed $400 million, with an average franchise unit generating ~$942K per year.

brancoptica.pt Brancóptica, Lda is a family-owned optical retail chain founded in 1961 in Cartaxo, Portugal (Ribatejo region) by José Francisco Branco de Oliveira, originally as "Oculista do Cartaxo." Now led by the founder's son Rui Oliveira, the company operates 20+ stores across three districts — Santarém, Lisbon, and Leiria — under the banner of the international Opticalia alliance (part of EssilorLuxottica). Beyond selling eyewear (Ray-Ban, Gucci, and designer brands), it provides professional optometry and orthoptics services with a team of 20+ qualified specialists, and runs its own e-commerce store on Shopify. The company employs roughly 31–51 people with estimated revenue in the €2–10 million range. It is a rare example of a family optical chain that has survived and grown amid the mass decline of independent opticians in Portugal, winning the ÓpticaPro 2024 Social Responsibility Award.

craisa.com zoominfo.com/c/craisa/345610542 CRAISA S.A. is a Costa Rican distributor of agricultural, construction, and industrial machinery, founded in 1981 and headquartered in Heredia. It is the official exclusive dealer of CASE IH (agriculture) and CASE Construction Equipment in Costa Rica, covering the entire country through branches in Heredia, San Carlos, Guápiles, and Cartago. The company also distributes specialty brands including Antonio Carraro (Italian specialty tractors), Hangcha (forklifts), XAG agricultural drones, and precision farming systems (Raven/Trimble), while offering in-house service workshops, genuine parts supply, and equipment financing. It employs around 43 people with a highly loyal management core (many directors with 15–22 years of tenure), operates under SAP Business One, and holds official "Carbono Neutral" certification from the Costa Rican government.

agrocampo.com.co zoominfo.com/c/agrocampo/433785602 Agrocampo S.A.S. is Colombia's first and only veterinary hypermarket, founded in 1979 by veterinarian Alfonso Villa and headquartered in Bogotá, serving as the country's leading distributor of veterinary drugs and agricultural supplies for over 45 years. The company operates one flagship hypermarket in Bogotá plus a 24/7 distribution center of ~8,000 m² in Cota, delivering 15,000+ products to ~980 municipalities (99% of Colombia's territory) through e-commerce, call center, and a network of partner veterinary stores it deliberately does not compete with. It generates around COP 164 billion (~USD 40 million) in annual revenue with a team of ~270–300 employees, and also operates in Panama, Guatemala, and Costa Rica.

markisol.se zoominfo.com/c/markisol-ab/357807356 Markisol Group is a Swedish family-owned manufacturer of window blinds (roller, venetian, pleated, roman, and panel) headquartered in Ronneby, Sweden, founded in the late 1960s by Bo Persson, who started making blinds at age 6 alongside his father and built the company into one of the world's leading blind producers. The company has been a supplier to IKEA since 1983 and is fully vertically integrated — it designs and builds its own patented assembly machines (up to 400 blinds per hour), produces its own components, and weaves and prints its own fabrics at its textile plant in Narva, Estonia (in the historic Krenholm factory).

trifectasoftware.com zoominfo.com/c/trifecta-software/464122642 Trifecta Software is a small Costa Rican software development company based in San José, founded in 2011 by Joseph Phillips, a Costa Rican engineer and entrepreneur. The company provides custom software development for U.S. clients (mostly under NDA), plus CRM implementation based on open-source vTiger (branded CostaRicaCRM), and operates within a family of related businesses including a digital marketing agency (Mercadeo Asertivo) and an e-invoicing SaaS (Facturero.com). Its founder previously co-founded a health-tech startup that was acquired by Huli Health in 2018. The team is small — around 6 people — with revenue estimated between $250K and $1.5 million annually. In November 2025, the company registered a new legal entity in Panama, and in 2026 repositioned itself with an "AI-first" custom software branding.

anphealthsolutions.com ANP Health Services Inc. is a Florida-based recruitment agency specializing in placing foreign-trained nurses into U.S. hospitals, with a strong focus on Latin America (especially Venezuela). Founded in 2019 by Nelson Hurtado, a Venezuelan immigrant and registered nurse, the company provides an end-to-end service: credential validation, NCLEX exam preparation, English training, direct-hire placement with 150+ partner hospitals, and visa sponsorship (EB-3 Green Card for the nurse and family). It has helped over 2,000 nurses from 28 countries, with candidates typically earning $70–100K per year plus sign-on bonuses. The company is a Certified Ethical Recruiter (CGFNS Alliance) — one of only about 16 accredited firms in the U.S. — and employs roughly 30–50 people across 9 countries. Estimated revenue is $10–50 million annually.

progenyag.com zoominfo.com/c/progeny-ag/351504348 Erwin-Keith, Inc. (Progeny Ag Products) is a family-owned seed and grain company founded in 1984 in the Arkansas Delta (Wynne, Arkansas, USA), operating under the Progeny brand since 1997. The company develops and markets its own varieties of soybeans, corn, wheat, and rice, selling across 10–11 Southern U.S. states. Its rice brand ProGold is licensed from the University of Arkansas — and ProGold L4 and M3 varieties are now included in the university's official 2026 recommended planting list. Beyond seeds, the company runs grain elevators (including a rail facility), a trucking fleet across 9 states, and grain marketing programs (HTA, basis-only, and average pricing contracts). Estimated revenue is around $26 million with roughly 100+ employees (seasonal workforce included), and the business remains led by the founding Erwin and Keith families.

grupomarsan.com zoominfo.com/c/grupo-marsan/460771135 Grupo Marsan is a Spanish Tier 2 automotive supplier founded in 1951 in Vigo, Spain, specializing in industrial surface coatings — cataphoresis (e-coating), powder and liquid painting — plus metal stamping, assembly, and JIT logistics, with a capacity of 300,000 parts per day. The company operates plants in Spain (Vigo, Zaragoza), Portugal, and Mexico, and also builds and runs dedicated in-house coating lines inside clients' facilities, supported by its own technology center M-Tech. It works under IATF automotive quality standards within supply chains of major OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers. After a liquidity crisis in 2024, the group was recapitalized with private and Galician public funds (~47.5% held by Xesgalicia and Vigo Activo), and Marcos Oubiña was appointed CEO. FY2024 revenue exceeded €28 million with ~450 employees, and in 2025 the company acquired KATA Aragón, growing to ~500 employees

guardrisk.co.za  rocketreach.co/guardrisk-insurance-company-ltd-profile_b5a52494f9c62c8e Guardrisk is a South African specialist insurance group, founded in 1993 and widely recognized as the pioneer and market leader of cell captive insurance in Africa — a model that allows companies to run their own "branded" insurance business under Guardrisk's licensed infrastructure instead of building a full insurer themselves. Headquartered in Sandton, Johannesburg, the group operates licensed insurers for life, non-life, and microinsurance, plus international cells in Mauritius and Gibraltar, and employs around 530 people. It has been wholly owned since 2013–14 by Momentum Group (JSE: MTN-listed MTM), which acquired it for R1.6 billion. For the financial year ended 30 June 2025, Guardrisk managed total assets of R68 billion and over 240 active cells, generating net revenue of ~R2 billion and pre-tax trading profit of ~R1 billion

metalware.ca zoominfo.com/c/metalware-corp/57640606 Metalware Corporation is a Canadian manufacturer of industrial steel shelving and storage systems, based in Montreal, Quebec, and in business since the early 1950s. The company is best known as the inventor of boltless ("No-Bolt") shelving, patented in 1954 by founders Irving and Ben Levitt — a design that became the industry standard for order-picking warehouses. Still family-owned and led by second/third-generation owners (President Mark Levitt), Metalware produces its flagship Interlok No-Bolt line, E-Series widespan shelving, multi-tier/high-bay systems, shelf-supported mezzanines, and modular drawer solutions at its Montreal plant, selling through a network of authorized distributors across North America. Its reference clients include the Government of Canada (Canada Revenue Agency, Department of National Defence), Porsche, and Walmart

st.com zoominfo.com/c/stmicroelectronics/114508234 Revenue $13.1 Billion STMicroelectronics (ST) is one of the world's largest semiconductor companies and Europe's biggest chipmaker, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. Formed in 1987 through the merger of Italian and French state-owned chip companies, it is a fully integrated manufacturer — it designs, produces, and sells its own chips. Its core products are microcontrollers (the flagship STM32 family), sensors, analog and power chips, silicon carbide devices for electric vehicles, and chips for data centers and satellites. The company serves over 200,000 customers worldwide — including Apple, Tesla, Bosch, Samsung, and SpaceX — supplying components for cars, smartphones, industrial equipment, and data centers. It operates 14 manufacturing plants across Europe and Asia, employs about 49,000 people, and invests roughly 17% of its revenue in R&D.

fachhandel-hell.at Hell Helmut GmbH is a small family-owned B2B wholesale company based in Hall in Tirol, Austria, operating for over 20 years and specialized in sanitary and heating supplies. The company positions itself as a system supplier for underfloor heating, serving professional installers across Tyrol, Vorarlberg, and Salzburg. It sources directly from leading manufacturers — primarily IMI Heimeier (thermostatic and balancing valves) and Uponor (underfloor heating and drinking water systems) — guaranteeing original quality. Its key differentiator is in-house prefabrication: ready-made manifold stations and water metering stations built exclusively from IMI and Uponor components. The business is 100% owned and personally managed by its founder Helmut Hell, with a lean team of about 5–6 people. Overall, it is a classic regional specialist wholesaler: small, owner-run, and focused on system-based project supply rather than retail.

magnetos.com.mx zoominfo.com/c/magnetos-y-refacciones-sa-de-cv/1288761434 Magnetos y Refacciones, S.A. de C.V. is a Mexican trading and service company founded in 1977 and headquartered in Guadalajara, Jalisco. Its core business is supplying magnet wire, bearings, insulating varnishes, electric motors, and spare parts for motor repair — wholesale and retail, serving customers across all 32 Mexican states. Its second key business is a nationwide network of authorized service centers performing warranty and post-warranty repair for Groupe SEB brands (Krups, T-Fal, Rowenta, Moulinex) and Taurus in 8–10 Mexican cities. The company employs around 129 people and is part of a small group operated by Corporación Rodaja. It also exports to Central America (mainly El Salvador), with about US$4.2 million in shipments over the last five years. Despite nearly 50 years on the market, it has virtually no digital presence — its website is an empty placeholder.
